comments.author: @Urgelt
comments.text:
Day trading is already disadvantageous for humans. Algorithms and knowledge are not on retail investors' side.

Where algorithms and knowledge of the pros falters is in long-term stock performance. Humans still have a chance - because uncertainty is vast, and because the pros are focused on quarterly results. They'll pass on payoffs too far outside of their performance windows.

The pros won't use AI agents for long-term investing. But retail investors probably will. Which might mean that long-term invrsting could become as disadvantageous for retail investors not using agents as day trading alteady is.

comments.author: @draken5379
comments.text:
Its weird. Its peoples people are totally forgotten or missed the GPT2 era ?

Seeing a lot of hype around 'give examples and LLM works better', and 'agents'.

These two concepts arnt new. They have been around since GPT2, and are pretty much how LLMs are already used. ChatGPT, IS an 'agent'. You arnt interacting directly with the LLM, you are interacting with an Agent designed by OpenAI.

'Few shot' prompting, aka, giving examples, has also been around for 2+ years, and its used a lot to get the LLM to output how you want.
